title: Gratitude to the New Orleans Jazz Club and listening to every player
summary: He credits the club and its members, and says to listen to every player since each has something to offer.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: You know, that all that stuff is lurking in your brain there someplace, George. So, yeah, you're playing fairly regularly now with all these traditional bands all around the Bay Area. Your 70th birthday was a big event at the New Orleans Jazz Club. So what do you think about all this? All these people still playing this fairly ancient music these days? You know, do you enjoy it? Do you, you know, what's your view of this whole scene?

Well, I think the New Orleans Jazz Club was very instrumental in keeping this alive. And I will always be indebted to them, I would say, in that way and respect them because they have done a lot for me and recognition and many others. And Dottie Lawless, if I may call her name, or see Ed and Dottie Lawless, and Ori Collins and many others have been very instrumental in helping me to, what I'd say, come back into the traditional, playing traditional jazz again.

Don't you sit there, though, George, you know, and you hear somebody lumbering through a bad trombone solo and you say, that isn't the way Louie Nelson played it, you know? What does this guy think he's doing?
Well, no, because like a trumpet player, they've always told me, regardless of how bad a guy played, he will play something that you can't play.

And so always listen to him because that time will come that you can't play what he's playing. And so I go along, so I've always been able to listen to whoever is performing because if he spend any time at all playing a horn, he has something to offer.

Well, you're real enthusiastic. You encourage everybody. I think you're one of the few musicians around that actually, you even give little instructions once in a while and lead a riff and get things going. You know, you really contribute when you're playing. And, you know, I think people really appreciate that. Thank you.
I try to. I enjoy playing. And I've been very fortunate enough to meet so many nice people.

Like you, Mel, you're a very good friend of mine. Sure. And you have helped me a lot and I appreciate it. And when I play with you, you seem to put so much in your playing. You play from your heart. Right. And this makes me feel good. It just goes right through you from the top to the bottom. I mean, from your little tool look like it. I've seen you with those shoes. All the little tube you get to trickle when you're playing. And this is what it's all about.
